items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Dave Frishberg is one of the best lyricists I’ve ever written with

ctx.x: “You Are There,” is just one of those songs that emerged one morning, I was on my way to an appointment and I stopped the car and wrote it down, it all came out in one – it’s the kind of a song that you’d never set out to write and I didn’t know what to do with that song, I had five different lyrics to it before Dave Frishberg came up with the – and he wrote the last two of them. I got… three of them before and they just didn't make it, they didn’t even come close.

Frishberg took it, he wrote a lyric and he said, “Nah, I can do better than that,” so he wrote and then next one he wrote was, “You Are There.” And Dave Frishberg is one of the best lyricists I’ve ever written with, he can do anything. He’s as close to Johnny Mercer as you can get.

items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: like Johnny Mandel called me about a month ago before I came on this trip that I’m on now, and told me that he needed some material for a new record he was producing

ctx.x: That one took years. Not because it took years, because I carried the title around in my head for years before I ever acted on it. But I remember thinking that would be a great title. And then I never really followed through on it. I had it in mind for a decade though. But otherwise it depends. If I’m under the gun, and believe it or not there are situations even in today’s music business where I might be under the gun, like Johnny Mandel called me about a month ago before I came on this trip that I’m on now, and…
